text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Trading at the Amsterdam Stock Exchange and EOE Options Exchange halted yesterday as private investors pulled out in panic. (p1)
- Shipping and road haulage group Nedlloyd optimistic despite halved 1996 net profit. (p1)
- Average price of existing residential home falls from Dfl 238,163 in December to Dfl 233,298 in January. (p1)
- Chairman of potato starch company Avebe resigns unexpectedly. (p1)
- Bath room producer Sphinx Gustavsberg is to restructure even more deeply as 1996/1997 bookyear shows red figures. (p1)
- Technical service provider GTI Holding sees 1996 profit rise 30 pct to Dfl 25.6 million. (p3)
- Parliament is critical about PTT Telecom's plans to offer a free E-mail address to its subscribers. (p3)
- Trading and engineering group Internatio-Mueller posts 15 pct higher 1996 net despite lower medicine prices. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Foreign affairs minister Hans van Mierlo wants to send EU- police force to Albania. (p1)
- Amsterdam Exchanges in favour of "big bang" conversion to Euro single currency on January 4, 1999. (p2)
- Paper and packaging group KNP BT enters the Asian market. (p2)
- Chemicals concern Akzo Nobel is to modernise its U.S. subsidiary McCook of Illinois for $50 million. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Move of shippping concern NCS/Eurosal to ports of Rotterdam and Zeebrugge is a severe blow for Amsterdam. (p7)
- Newspaper publisher De Telegraaf's bid for Financieele Dagblad rejected. (p25)
- Dutch economic growth is 1996 was 2.7 pct according to central statistics bureau CBS. (p27)
- Cheap diesel for trucking sector not until 1999. (p27)
TROUW
- Health minister Els Borst admists having made mistakes with home care reorganisation. (p1)
- Liberal party VVD tired of waiting for a decision on the extension of Amsterdam Schiphol Airport. (p4)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Royal Dutch Arlines/KLM rows with Belgium's carrier VLM about unfair competition. (p11)
- Akzo Nobel to cut jobs at its Delfzijl plant. (p13)
-- Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
